Scripture integrity, made visible.

VERSE ONE 2.0 · Foundation pilot · 15 November 2026 IST

Status: six editions imported and compared to the downloaded publisher exports. This is not a production certification.

What these checks establish

Every imported verse label and verse body matches the corresponding USFM source after documented formatting normalization. USFX supplies the reader data; a separate USFM parser supplies the comparison. Every chapter and verse-label inventory is checked between these two exports. Source archives and installable packs carry SHA-256 fingerprints. The two formats originate from the same publisher and are not independent textual witnesses.

What “complete” means here

The imported collection covers the 66 selected Protestant books in each downloaded edition. No imported chapter or verse unit is omitted relative to that source collection. It does not establish absence of errors in the publisher’s edition, correctness against manuscripts, or Catholic/Orthodox completeness. We use “source-compared,” not an unrestricted “verified Bible” badge.

Numbering differences and source caveats

Combined verse labels stay combined. A search for a number inside a bridge returns the complete source passage and its actual label. No cross-edition equivalence mapping is claimed. English has five empty source verse bodies; the reader explains these without inventing words. Source notes remain accessible. The English USFX archive includes extra books despite its Protestant metadata; only the 66 books also represented in the chosen USFM collection are imported. Excluded source identifiers are listed below.

Conversion policy

No AI-generated Scripture. No spelling, punctuation, vocabulary or translation corrections. Formatting whitespace is consolidated. Notes and headings are separated from verse bodies; their words are retained. Typography, original paragraph/poetry layout, lexical attributes and front/back matter are not fully rendered in this pilot; original source archives are included. This is a reading representation, not a facsimile.

Licensing and missing editions

WEBP text is public domain. The five IRV datasets are CC BY-SA 4.0; their notices and attribution are retained. VERSE ONE’s converted IRV data contributions are provided under CC BY-SA 4.0. Neither translation owner endorses this application. KJV, ASV, copyrighted commercial versions, additional languages and other canons are not included. No licensing fee was incurred.

Offline and access limits

After a successful installation, edition data and indexes live in IndexedDB. Installation verifies checksum and size before committing. The application shell is cached by a service worker on localhost or HTTPS. Browser eviction, user deletion, disk capacity and private browsing can affect persistence. This package is local-only, has no server authentication, and must not be publicly deployed as a private church system.
